item.title: INP: how fast the page answers a tap.
item.description:
Word of the day: INP: how fast the page answers a tap.
Interaction to Next Paint measures the delay from a click, tap or key press to the next frame on screen. It replaced First Input Delay as a Core Web Vital in March 2024.
Spot it: Find the slowest tap on your page, often a menu or a filter, and break up the long task behind it.

item.title: Mozilla: 85 languages, no sitemap.
item.description:
The home page lists 85 hreflang alternates, HSTS is on, and framing is denied. But robots.txt names no sitemap and /sitemap.xml answers 404, so crawlers find pages only by following links.
The lesson for every team: Publish a sitemap.xml of the pages you want found and name it in robots.txt with one Sitemap: line.

item.title: See your page the way Googlebot does.
item.description:
30-second trick: See your page the way Googlebot does.
Search Console's URL Inspection tool can fetch a live page as Google and show the rendered HTML, a screenshot, and the resources it could not load.
Try it now: Search the rendered HTML for your main heading and your key facts. If they are missing there, Google may not see them either.

#SEO #SoftwareTesting #DevOps #QA #TechnicalSEO #QAlab

item.title: Myth: a sitemap gets every page indexed.
item.description:
Myth vs fact: Myth: a sitemap gets every page indexed.
A sitemap helps search engines discover your pages. Google says plainly that it does not guarantee every listed page will be crawled and indexed.
Check it: Open the Pages report in Search Console and filter it by your sitemap. Each page left out is listed with its reason.

item.title: Wikipedia leaves the snippet to search.
item.description:
HSTS is preloaded, security.txt is published, and articles read without JavaScript. But the Main Page and the other 18 pages analyzed have no meta description, so search engines pick the snippet.
The lesson for every team: Write a description of about 150 characters for each key page, so you choose the pitch, not the crawler.
One automated analysis of public pages on 19 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict. How the review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=runs-100-2026-11&utm_content=wikipedia
#SEO #MetaDescription #OpenKnowledge #QA #QAlab

item.title: NASA is wide open to AI search.
item.description:
GEO scores 91: answer crawlers are welcome, structured data names the organization, and pages carry authors and dates. Security headers are where it trails.
The lesson for every team: Four headers close most of that gap: Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy.
One automated analysis of public pages on 19 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict. How the review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=runs-2026-10&utm_content=nasa

item.title: 3 natural competitors. A tie at the top: 78.
item.description:
tradersunion.com leads in SEO, GEO, Analytics; trygghansa.se leads in Security, Performance; if.se leads in Accessibility.
The lesson for every team: Benchmark against the sites your visitors compare you with, not against a perfect score: the gap that costs you is the one a competitor has already closed.

item.title: vitibet.com: 59. The gap: alt text.
item.description:
Every internal link that was opened answered, and model-training crawlers are blocked by choice. But 2097 images have no alt attribute.
The lesson for every team: Describe what each image shows in its alt attribute, and use alt="" on purely decorative ones.

item.title: lexter.ai: 63. The gap: text contrast.
item.description:
Every page has a title, and AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page. But elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds.
The lesson for every team: Keep body text at a 4.5:1 contrast ratio or more against its background.

item.title: mono.la: 81. The gap: framing.
item.description:
Every internal link that was opened answered, and AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page. But other sites can frame the page.
The lesson for every team: Send frame-ancestors 'self' in the CSP, or X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, so other sites cannot frame your pages.
